questions.question: Which of the following was only the authority of the state in the period of Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mines.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mines** were the only** authority of the state** in the **period of Maurya.**
 
• Mines and materials extracted from it like **gold, silver, copper, iron and tin **were the sole authority of the state.
 
• It was **used to manufacture weapons and armour **for the king's military campaign.
 
• It also provided the needed metal** to maintain currency.**
 
• It was imperative to **control the mining** to stabilize the flow of currency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Mauryan Empire**

 
• The **Maurya dynasty (321–185 BC) **was a powerful dynasty in ancient India.
 
• The Maurya dynasty ruled India **for 137 years.**
 
• The credit for its establishment is given to** Chandragupta Maurya and his minister Chanakya (Kautilya).**
 
• This empire started from the plains of the **Ganges river (today's Bihar and Bengal)** in the state of **Magadha** in the east.
 
• Its **capital was Pataliputra **(near present-day Patna city).
 
• Chandragupta Maurya established this empire in **321 BC **and rapidly expanded his kingdom towards the west.
 
• The Mauryan Empire grew and** thrived during the Iron Age.**
 
• He took advantage of the differences between several small regional kingdoms that had arisen after Alexander's invasion.
 
• **By 316 BC,** the Maurya dynasty had occupied the** whole of North Western India.**
 
• The Maurya dynasty **expanded on a large scale** during the reign of the** Chakravarti emperor Ashoka.**
 
• Due to Emperor Ashoka, the Maurya Empire became the most significant and powerful.

questions.question: What is the national flower of Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
Shalpa (Water Lily) is the national flower of Bangladesh.

 
• It is indigenous to southern and eastern parts of Asia and is the national flower of Sri Lanka as well.
 
• It is used as an ornamental plant because of its spectacular flowers, and is most commonly used for the traditional and cultural festivals in Bangladesh as well as Sri Lanka.
 
• It is also used as a food item and included in many dishes of Bangladeshi cuisine.

questions.question: Which of the following has largest atomic radius?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Li.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lithium has the largest atomic radius i.e. **167pm.**
 
• Whereas, **Beryllium – 112 pm,** **Boron – 87 pm,** and **Oxygen – 48** pm are smaller than Lithium.
 
• Atomic radius is the measure of the size of the atom of a particular chemical element.
 
• The measurement from the center of the nucleus to the boundary of the surrounded electron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Atomic radius - 

 
 
• It is the distance between the nucleus of an atom to its outermost electron that is called the 'Atomic Radius'.
 
• The exact value of the atomic radius of an atom cannot be known.
 
• Because the atom is not found in a free state nor can the exact position of the electron be known.​
 
• In general, the atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group.

questions.question: Out of all known elements, the minimum number is of _________ in the periodic table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metalloids.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Concept

__
 
• Metalloids are elements that exhibit properties of both metals and non-metals.
 
• They are placed at the zigzag borderline separating metals and non-metals in the periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca91a54e65799f678b3f8bf47120fb3a319d5adf7fa456f92d1da636d2154681.png] 

Explanation

 
• Silicon(Si), Germanium (Ge), Antimony(Sb), Tellurium(Te), Polonium(Po) are metalloids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Non-metals-**

 
• Non Metals are generally found in solid or gaseous form.
 
• They are not lustrous and are bad conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• They can not be converted into thin sheets.
 
• The most common example of non-metal is Carbon. Carbon belongs to Group 14 of the Modern periodic table. It has atomic number 6 and has four electrons in its outermost shell. It is tetravalent i.e. it can form four bonds by sharing its outermost electrons.

**Metals-**

 
• Metals are substances that form naturally below the **surface of the Earth**. Most metals are lustrous or **shiny**. Metals are **inorganic**, which means they are made of substances that were never alive.
 
• All metals are **good conductors of heat and electricity**. Cooking utensils and irons are made up of metals as they are good conductors of heat.
 
• **Ductility** is the ability of the material to be stretched into a wire.

questions.question: The concept of suspension of fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution has been taken from which country’s constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Germany.**__

**Explanation:**

The concept of suspension of fundamental rights during an emergency is taken from **Germany.**

There are **three types** of emergencies: 

__
 
• National Emergency
 
• Failure of constitutional machinery in states
 
• Financial Emergency

**National Emergency: Article 352** of the Indian Constitution talks about the national emergency. A national emergency is imposed whereby there is a grave threat to the security of India or any of its territories due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. Such emergency shall be imposed by the president on the basis of a written request by the council of ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

**State Emergency:** **Article 356** talks about the failure of constitutional machinery in a state also known as the President’s rule. If the president on Governor’s report or otherwise is satisfied that the situation has arisen that the government can’t be carried in accordance with the constitutional provisions then, he may issue a State emergency.

**Financial Emergency: **The president under **Article 360** of the constitution has the power to declare a financial emergency if he is satisfied that the financial stability or the credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened. It has to be laid before both the Houses of Parliament and ceases to operate at the expiration of two months unless meanwhile approved by the resolution of Houses.

**About other options:**

 **Russia**
 Fundamental Duties, Idea of Social, Economic, and Political justice in the Preamble

questions.question: Which Part of Indian constitution contains Article 368 that gives power to the parliament to do constitutional amendments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Part __**XX**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 368 which gives the power of amendment is enshrined in Part XX of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• Part XX has only one article i.e. Art 368 that deals with the amendment of the constitution.
 
• As per Art 368Parliament may add, amend, or repeal any provision of the constitution as per the procedure laid down for this purpose except the one that comes under the basic structure of the constitution
 
 
• .After duly passed by both the Houses of Parliament and ratified by the state legislatures, where necessary, the bill is presented to the President for assent.
 
• The President must give his assent to the bill. He can neither withhold his assent to the bill nor return the bill to the Parliament for reconsideration.
 
• **After the President’s assent, the bill becomes an Act (i.e., a Constitutional Amendment Act) and the Constitution stands amended in accordance with the terms of the Act.**

questions.question: Plants of which group are predominantly aquatic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thallophyta.**__

__**Explanation:**__

Thallophyta:

 
• Thallophytes are organisms that possess a thallus-like body.
 
• The body is not differentiated into stems, roots and leaves.
 
• They are tracheophytes (vascular tissues are absent).
 
• Lichens and algae fall under thallophyta.

 Bryophyta:

 
• They are tracheophytes, archegoniate, and amphibious cryptogams.
 
• Various mosses and liverworts fall under the classification of Bryophyta.
 
• They are commonly found growing in moist and shaded areas in the hills.
 
• Bryophytes can live in the soil, but they depend on water for sexual reproduction.
 
• They have a thallus-like body and possess rootlike and leaf-like structures.
 
• Their main plant body is haploid.

 Pteridophyta:

 
• They are archegoniate, embryophytes, tracheophytes cryptogams.
 
• Ferns and horsetails fall under the Pteridophyta.
 
• They are found growing in cool, damp, shady places. They also grow well in sandy soils.
 
• Evolutionarily they are the first plants to possess the vascular system- xylem and phloem.

questions.question: Carbon dioxide is one of the gases that cause the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a __**Greenhouse effect.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Solar energy is trapped by the earth's atmosphere and radiates slowly so as to cover our earth with a warm blanket.
 
• This is the natural process of the greenhouse effect on earth to maintain its temperature and makes the earth perfect for life.
 
• A greenhouse gas (GHG or GHG) is a gas that absorbs and emits radiant energy within the thermal infrared range, causing the greenhouse effect.
 
• The primary greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere are water vapour (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and ozone (O3).
 
• ​Coal, oil, and natural gas are fossil fuel which is utilized for transportation and electricity generation among others.
 
• These gases form the insulation that keeps the planet warm enough to support life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd5c44b5cf473234011f68ec41886c08c55ca3faf9b62e29e211de08b831c1dd.png] 

Explanation:__

__
 
• Carbon dioxide is emitted whenever coal, oil, natural gas, and other carbon-rich fossil fuels are burned. 
 
• It is the largest contributor to climate change.
 
• Methane is caused by the decomposition of plant matter and is released from landfills, swamps, and rice paddies.
 
• Nitrous oxide is released from bacteria in the soil.​
 
• ​__Thus, CO2 is one of the major greenhouse gases. Methane, Nitrous Oxide are other gases that cause green house effect.

questions.question: In Microsoft Excel, down arrow key stroke leads to _________ cell movement on spreadsheet.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**One cell down.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Microsoft Excel, the down arrow key leads to the One Cell down movement.
 
• Just like the down key, every arrow key performs the same function i.e. right arrow key when pressed leads to one cell's right movement, the left arrow key lead to one cell's left movement, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• MS Excel, a spreadsheet program, is widely used for varied functions, as a result, the info is simple to avoid wasting time, and data is accessible and removed with zero discomforts and less labour.
 
• Cells: MS Excel consists of rows and columns which form cells. The cells are formed by intersecting rows and columns. Each cell can hold text, numbers, special characters, and so on. The rows of MS Excel are named after numbers (e.g. 1,2,3,4...) and the columns are named with capital letters (e.g. A, B, C, D, ...). There are 16,384 columns and 10,48,576 rows in the MS Excel sheet. The very first cell of MS Excel is named A1.
 
• Grids: In MS Excel, the cells can be differentiated by the grid lines. The gridline of the cells can be modified as per the requirement. The size of the cells also can be adjusted by moving the gridlines.
 
• Worksheet: The worksheet is referred to as the working area of MS Excel. It is also named a spreadsheet. The worksheet in MS Excel is filled with cells. In the worksheet, the user can perform mathematical calculations, store data, and so on.
 
• Workbook: After storing the data in MS Excel, the user saves the file with a proper name. This file is referred to as a workbook. The workbook can hold at least one or many worksheets.
